uncited: Unlike its siblings, NeRF-W explicitly models both appearance and transient geometry simultaneously, whereas [Aug-NeRF](10294-aug-nerf.md) focuses on robustness via perturbations, [NeRF Ensemble with Conjoint Pruning](12608-nerf-ensemble-with-conjoint-pruning.md) on compression, and [ContraNeRF](13659-contranerf.md) on cross-view consistency without per-scene optimization.

*   **Outputs:** Rendered color $\hat{C}_i(\mathbf{r})$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}$; static density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$, static color $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$, transient density $\sigma_i^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{x})$, transient color $\mathbf{c}_i^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$, and uncertainty variance $\beta_i(\mathbf{x})^2$.
Outputs static density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ and intermediate features $\mathbf{z}(\mathbf{x})$.
**Appearance Embedding ($\mathbf{l}_i^{(a)}$):** A learnable vector of length $n^{(a)}$ for each image $i$.
**Transient MLP ($MLP_{\theta_3}$):** Takes $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{d}$, and a transient embedding $\mathbf{l}_i^{(\tau)}$ (length $n^{(\tau)}$).
Outputs transient density $\sigma_i^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{x})$ and transient color $\mathbf{c}_i^{(\tau)}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$.
**Sampling:** For each training image $I_i$, sample rays $\mathbf{r}$.
**Static Query:** For each point $t_k$, query $MLP_{\theta_1}$ to get $\sigma(t_k)$ and $\mathbf{z}(t_k)$.
The first two terms are the negative log-likelihood of the color difference assuming Gaussian noise with variance $\beta_i(\mathbf{r})^2$.
*   **Time and Memory Complexity:** Training requires optimizing per-image embeddings ($N$ vectors) alongside MLP weights, increasing memory usage compared to standard NeRF.
